description: Last real conclusion of every job in every push/pull_request workflow. The object list is discovered by parsing .github/workflows, not enumerated here, because the enforcement surface ledger only classifies scripts/qa/* and would never have looked at boundary-coverage, test, clippy, miri or cross-compile. Verified offline by scripts/qa/ci-liveness.rb in the ci.yml governance job; refreshed from `gh run` locally with --refresh --write.

knownFailing.reason: Bootstrap, and it closes itself. The governance job's only failing gate is ci-liveness.rb, and it fails for two reasons this branch cannot fix: every ci.yml record expired when FR-174 edited the workflow, and nightly-governance.yml exists on disk having never run. It cannot run until this merges — GitHub registers a workflow_dispatch workflow only from the default branch (measured: HTTP 404, and absent from the workflows API). Every other gate in the job passed, at tier `full`, with 19 meta-verification gates read and none skipped. Remove this annotation in the same commit as the post-merge `ci-liveness.rb --refresh --write`; the gate enforces that itself, since an annotation outliving its failure reports 'marked known-failing but last concluded success'.

RUSTSEC-2026-0258, `h2` 0.4.15, 'unbounded empty DATA frames'; the fix is >=0.4.16 and h2 is transitive. Not caused by this branch, which touches no Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock: cargo audit fetches the advisory database live, so the failure is time-varying rather than branch-varying — the same commit passed on main's last four runs, before this advisory was published. Remove when the h2 bump lands; it needs its own change and must not be absorbed into FR-174.

workflows.reason: triggered by v* tags and workflow_dispatch only, so it has no last-run-on-main to assert. A release that fails is visible at the moment someone cuts it, and recording a stale tag build here would say less than nothing.

Added by FR-174 and has never run, so there is no real conclusion to record and this ledger holds only real runs — writing a headSha for a run that did not happen is the entry it exists to prevent. It cannot run before this merges: GitHub registers a workflow_dispatch workflow only from the default branch (measured: `gh workflow run --ref <branch>` returns HTTP 404 'not found on the default branch', and it is absent from the workflows API), and a scheduled trigger fires only on the default branch too. **This exclusion is the exact opposite of what FR-174 requires and must not survive the merge**: requirement 2 is that every gate moved off the PR path has verifiable execution evidence, and an inScope:false nightly is that claim going unchecked — the DD-159 shape, a gate presenting 'unverified' as 'passed'. Flip to inScope:true and record a real run immediately after the first nightly fires. FR-174 stays In Progress until then, and that is what tracks this.
